note: Keyword codebook defined by the author: four dimensions, generations 2 to 4. Terms joined with / are counted together. Generation 1 is not included because almost all of that generation has died and cannot be interviewed.

dimensions.label: Fear and risk
dimensions.question: What did this generation worry about most?

dimensions.label: Mobility and agency
dimensions.question: What helped them change their lives?

dimensions.label: Migration
dimensions.question: Why did they leave where they were?

dimensions.label: Historical change
dimensions.question: Which words tie the story to its times?

themes_note: Themes group codebook terms across dimensions so the same topic can be followed from one generation to the next. A term listed in several dimensions of one generation is counted once, using its largest count.

themes.label: Class and politics
themes.note: The centre of generation 2’s story: the class label, land reform, confiscation. In the family account the label decided who could go to school, and it was lifted only in 1981, when generation 3 was eight. None of these words are among the keywords of the two later generations.

themes.label: War and flight
themes.note: Only generation 2 lived through war. The flight to Cili County in 1945 is the first move the family records.

themes.label: Hometown and kin
themes.note: Generation 2 names the places it left and asks whether it kept in touch, after eighteen years without contact. Generation 3 speaks of 老家, the old home. For generation 4 the hometown words drop out of the list.

themes.label: Schooling
themes.note: The one theme near the top for every generation. Its words change: 读书 (studying) leads for generation 2, 教育 and 高考 (education, the entrance exam) for generation 3, and 大学, 专业 and 申请 (university, major, applications) for generation 4. Schooling moves from a way out of the village, to a national exam, to an application abroad.

themes.label: Work and income
themes.note: Steady in the middle for all three generations, with different words each time: 工程, 建筑, 工厂 (engineering, construction, factory) for the steel-plant generation; 工资, 收入, 单位 (wages, income, work unit) for their children; 就业 and 实习 (employment, internships) for the grandchildren.

themes.label: The city and growth
themes.note: Rises to first place for generation 3, born in the steel town of Ezhou in 1973 and living in Wuhan from 1991: the words of reform, growth and the city. For generation 4, born in Wuhan, the city is where life starts, not where it is heading.

themes.label: Housing
themes.note: Not among generation 2’s keywords. It appears with generation 3, who reached working age as the 1998 housing reform turned homes into something to buy, and shrinks for generation 4, where it becomes a mortgage.

themes.label: Hardship and security
themes.note: Generation 2 speaks of 困难, hardship. Generation 3 speaks of 稳定 and 养老, stability and old-age care. The worry changes from getting through to holding on.

themes.label: Competition and pressure
themes.note: A small theme for generation 3 and near the top for generation 4. 内卷 (involution), a word that became common only around 2020, is part of how generation 4 describes itself.

themes.label: Abroad and the wider world
themes.note: Absent for the two older generations and first for generation 4. Migration no longer means leaving the village for the city. It means leaving the country, and asking what that does to 身份, identity.
